.github/workflows/ci.yml.origin: Truthful CI for a dormant public fork (upstream chrisrob11/ancestrydl plus one DAQT commit adapting browser launch for headless server operation): build the executable, vet, race-tested unit tests including the pin on the headless adaptation, golangci-lint at a pinned version, and a conventional-commit title check on pull requests.
.github/workflows/ci.yml.protects: An upstream sync or edit that stops the executable compiling on the Go the module requires, breaks a unit test, or drops the headless and no-sandbox launcher flags without which the fork cannot start a browser on the server.
.github/workflows/ci.yml.consumer: Pull-request admission (the build and lint jobs are required; the commit-title check runs only on pull requests and is not required) and the daqt-server CI health monitor, which reads the default-branch verdict.
.github/workflows/ci.yml.falsifier: pkg/ancestry/browser_test.go fails when either launcher flag is removed; the Go toolchain is taken from go.mod so the workflow cannot pin a Go that rejects the module (the previous workflow pinned 1.22 against a 1.24.0 module and could not have built); the provider refuses unpinned action references.
.github/workflows/ci.yml.rollback: git revert of the workflow change; the ruleset requiring the two jobs is removed with the provider API if a job has to be withdrawn.

removed.codecov upload: no consumer: the fork publishes no coverage anywhere and the upload needed a moving third-party action
removed..github/workflows/release.yml: retired in #2: no release object, no consumer, and it tagged before it tested
